newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end up but off highs on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end up but off highs on U.S. data.

text.p: 1630 GMT - Austrian bonds got off to a strong start on Monday but ended off early highs after the release of U.S. data indicating an increase in inflationary pressures and traders said buying interest was at a minimum.
"Hardly anyone is getting involved anymore," said one trader, attributing the lull to clients closing their books ahead of the year end.
* Latest 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 up 85 bps at 99.90 to yield 5.88 (6.00) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 99.58/68 to yield 5.93/5.91.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 up 50 bps at 103.20 to yield 4.69 (4.81) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 103.02/12 to yield 4.74/71 percent.
* AGB future up 38 bps at 106.15 on turnover of 1,367 lots.
* 10-year spread to German bunds steady at eight bps, five-year spread down one at 20 bps.
* Money market rates mixed with three-month VIBOR steady at 3.350 and overnight money slightly lower at 2.97/3.22. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
